blocks.prompt: 3 Prove that the vectors \(\underline{i} - 2\underline{j} + 3\underline{k}\), \(-2\underline{i} + 3\underline{j} - 4\underline{k}\) and \(\underline{i} - 3\underline{j} + 5\underline{k}\) are coplanar.
blocks.explanation:
A coplanarity proof.
We must show the three vectors lie in one plane.
Plan: three vectors are coplanar exactly when their scalar triple product is 0 (14.4.5); compute the determinant.
steps:
Given: \(\underline{a} = \underline{i} - 2\underline{j} + 3\underline{k}\), \(\underline{b} = -2\underline{i} + 3\underline{j} - 4\underline{k}\), \(\underline{c} = \underline{i} - 3\underline{j} + 5\underline{k}\).
To prove: \(\underline{a}, \underline{b}, \underline{c}\) are coplanar.
Method: \([\underline{a}\ \underline{b}\ \underline{c}] = 0\) if and only if the vectors are coplanar: the "box" on them is flat, so its volume is 0.

Write the determinant
\[[\underline{a}\ \underline{b}\ \underline{c}] = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & -2 & 3 \\ -2 & 3 & -4 \\ 1 & -3 & 5 \end{vmatrix}\]
Why: The rows are the components of \(\underline{a}\), \(\underline{b}\), \(\underline{c}\).

Conclude and check
\[\underline{c} = 3\underline{a} + \underline{b}\]
\[3\underline{a} + \underline{b} = (3 - 2)\underline{i} + (-6 + 3)\underline{j} + (9 - 4)\underline{k}\]
\[= \underline{i} - 3\underline{j} + 5\underline{k} \;\checkmark\]
Why: The triple product is 0, so the vectors are coplanar. As a check, \(\underline{c}\) is a combination of \(\underline{a}\) and \(\underline{b}\), so it lies in their plane.
blocks.final_answer: \([\underline{a}\ \underline{b}\ \underline{c}] = 0\). Hence proved: the three vectors are coplanar.
